channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: Family Is Thankful Their Baby, Given Weeks to Live on Christmas Eve, Now Brain Cancer-Free
item.description: A baby given weeks to live with aggressive brain cancer is cancer-free after treatment from a newly finished study. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Texans Work for Free on Farms That Aren’t Theirs to Send Others’ Kids to College
item.description: Texas volunteers farm land that is not theirs, unpaid, and the harvest sends local children to college. How you can help: Give a few hours to a community project that raises money for local scholarships. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The Portlanders Turning Rescued Food Into Restaurant-Quality Meals
item.description: Portland chefs turn surplus food that would be thrown away into restaurant-quality meals for people who need them. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Ask a local food rescue group whether it needs volunteers or surplus food. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
item.description: Rare brine lakes found more than a mile under the Red Sea may show what Earth's ancient oceans were like. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Roman Glass Among the Silk Road Treasures Unearthed in Nomadic Noble’s Tomb
item.description: A nomadic noble’s tomb in Mongolia held glass from Classical Rome, showing how far Silk Road trade reached. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Autos for Love’ Owners Delight in Giving Away Cars to Needy Neighbors
item.description: A Texas repair shop couple fix up donated cars and hand the keys to neighbours in need, and the giving keeps growing. How you can help: If you have a car you no longer need, ask a local charity whether it can be donated. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Land Returned to Native American Ownership 400 Years After the First Thanksgiving
item.description: About 126 acres of Cape Cod salt marsh are back in Native American ownership, 400 years after the Pilgrims arrived. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected
item.description: The Euclid space telescope, built to study the dark Universe, has found its first previously unknown comet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
item.description: Physicists held a single positron in a wall-free trap near absolute zero, opening new tests of antimatter. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: China's Shenzhou-24 carries Pakistan's first astronaut into space
item.description: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became Pakistan’s first astronaut, flying to China’s Tiangong station aboard Shenzhou-24. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Physicists just sent an unblockable message through a brick wall using gravity
item.description: Physicists sent a message through a brick wall using only gravity, an old elevator counterweight and a fine detector. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Miki Kawamura: a 19-year-old’s peace network brings ice cream to a Nobel summit
item.description: Miki Kawamura, 19, built a peace network and took it, with ice cream, to the World Summit of Nobel Peace Laureates. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Major Success Sees Viral Infections Fall 68% in Brazil After Releasing Wolbachia-Infected Mosquitoes
item.description: Releasing mosquitoes that carry Wolbachia bacteria cut mosquito-borne infections in Brazilian schoolchildren by 68%. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Empty standing water from pots, buckets and gutters at home, where mosquitoes breed. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Retired Teacher Turns Retired Musical Instruments into Bird Feeders (LOOK)
item.description: A retired Canadian teacher turns scrapped musical instruments into feeders for the birds around his home. How you can help: Put out a feeder and fresh water for birds through the winter. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A Childhood Promise Mobilizes ‘Thanksgiving Heroes,’ Serving Thousands Nationwide This Holiday
item.description: A boy’s promise to his mother grew into Thanksgiving Heroes, feeding 3,600 families in Utah alone this year. How you can help: Give a few groceries or an hour of your time to a holiday meal drive near you. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Charity Swaps Tuition Fees for Coconuts So Every Islander Can Afford School
item.description: A school in Micronesia accepts coconuts in place of tuition fees, so every island family can afford lessons. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck reveals an ingenious waterproofing trick
item.description: Pine tar and beeswax on a 2,200-year-old Roman wreck show how shipbuilders kept their hulls watertight. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Why a Viagra-like blood flow drug may open a new front against Alzheimer’s
item.description: In a trial, a daily tablet slowed decline by 31% over a year in early Alzheimer’s patients on no other drug for it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: 33 Kids Wrote Letters to a Wounded Veteran. 60 Years Later, His Son Is Searching to Thank Each One
item.description: In 1967, 33 schoolchildren wrote to a wounded Navy corpsman; his son is now finding each one to thank them. How you can help: Write a card to someone recovering in hospital or serving far from home. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Determined Volunteer Rescues Lost Toddler in the Desert: ‘She may not be our child, but she could be’
item.description: An Arizona grandfather out searching as a volunteer found a missing toddler in the cold desert night. How you can help: Ask your local search and rescue team how volunteers can sign up. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: One-of-a-Kind Refuge to 200,000 Walrus Protected Forever in Alaska
item.description: A stretch of Alaska’s Bering Sea coast that shelters up to 200,000 Pacific walrus is now permanently protected. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: The City That Kicked Out Cars Before It Was Cool
item.description: Pontevedra in Spain took cars out of its centre long before other cities, and even a taxi driver approves. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Swap one short car trip this week for walking or cycling. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: This tiny spider named after Stephen Colbert has a genome 50% larger than a human’s
item.description: A quarter-sized California trapdoor spider turns out to carry a genome about 50% larger than a human's. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: New Method Treats Severe Thumb Arthritis With Joint Replacement – Just like a New Hip or Shoulder
item.description: A new thumb joint implant is giving people with advanced arthritis the use of their hands back. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: If thumb arthritis limits your grip, ask a hand specialist about joint replacement options. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Extraordinary’ Drug May Actually Cure High Blood Pressure Caused by Hormones, And it’s FDA-Approved
item.description: A study found an already approved drug may treat a hormonal root cause of high blood pressure, with lasting relief. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: If your blood pressure stays high on treatment, ask your doctor about testing for a hormonal cause. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Breath of a Whale Captured by Drone Allows Full Genome Sequencing Without Intrusion
item.description: Drones caught a whale’s breath, and scientists read its full genome from it without touching the animal. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Who was buried in Westminster Abbey's Roman coffin? A 150-year mystery may be solved
item.description: New dating suggests the skeleton in Westminster Abbey’s Roman coffin was a medieval abbot, easing a 150-year puzzle. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: After 8 years in space, a groundbreaking X-ray telescope finally opens its eyes
item.description: An X-ray telescope bound for Mercury took its first observations after eight years and is beating expectations. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: CERN scientists finally find evidence of a particle decay so rare it took 40 years to detect
item.description: CERN physicists found the first evidence of a decay so rare it took 40 years of searching to see. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Montreal Is Harnessing Soothing Ocean Sounds to Combat Traffic Noise
item.description: A Montreal pocket park plays soothing ocean sounds to soften the traffic noise around it. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: CAR-T therapy helps stiff person syndrome patients walk and work again
item.description: In a Mayo Clinic trial, CAR-T therapy helped people with stiff person syndrome walk and return to work. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
item.description: Five centuries-old baobabs dug up without permits were stopped at export and are being replanted. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Waterless, Hyper-Efficient Machines That Clean Clothes With Carbon Dioxide
item.description: New machines clean clothes with recycled carbon dioxide instead of water, using far less energy. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Wash full loads on a cold cycle to save water and energy at home. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: Barbershops are using the trust of their chairs to bring health checks to Black men who skip the doctor. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Book a routine blood pressure check if you have not had one this year. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: After the 2023 fires, Maui is asking visitors to help restore land and culture instead of just sightseeing. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: On your next trip, give a day to a local restoration or community project. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A German founder grows moss walls that cool and clean city air, starting from a fight to save one tree. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: In Alaska’s capital, food comes by water, air or, most often, community sharing
item.description: In Juneau, Alaska, neighbours feed each other by sharing fish, game and garden harvests. How you can help: Share extra garden produce or a meal with a neighbour this week. Source: The Guardian Environment.
